**Given:** AC and exactly the mesh, stabilization, time, exponent, flux, data and initialization hypotheses in the energy/compactness lemma.

[F1] [[lem-hybrid-mimetic-backward-euler-energy-and-compactness]] proves step existence, uniform energy and dual-time-derivative bounds, strong cell-state convergence in $L^r(H)$ for every finite $r$ and in $L^p(Q)$, and weak $G_h\overline U_h\rightharpoonup\nabla u$ with $u\in L^p(V)\cap L^\infty(H)$.

[F2] [[lem-fv-conforming-companion-and-test-recovery]] gives bounded mean tests, $G_hI_h\varphi\to\nabla\varphi$ uniformly and $S_{h,p}(I_h\varphi)=O(h)$ for smooth compactly supported spatial tests. [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]] gives growth and pointwise monotonicity.

[F3] [[lem-pe12-evolution-energy-chain-rule]] gives a continuous $H$ representative and the exact energy identity for a $V$-valued limit with derivative in $L^{p'}(V^*)$. [[lem-pe12-minty-identification]] identifies a weak constitutive-field limit from the weak gradients and the flux-energy limsup.

[F4] [[lem-mimetic-fv-parabolic-limit-identification]] applies to bounded open domains, conforming reconstructions and its explicitly stated residual/limsup hypotheses. Hölder estimates used below are [[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]].

[F5] [[thm-reflexivity-of-lp-for-one-less-p-less-infinity]] and [[cor-reflexive-iff-every-bounded-sequence-has-a-weakly-convergent-subsequence]] supply weak subsequences of bounded $L^r$ fields for $1<r<\infty$ under AC (coordinatewise for vector fields).



1.1 Use [F1] to extract the strong cell-state and weak-gradient subsequence. Growth gives $\|q_h\|_{L^{p'}(Q)}\le C(\|g\|_{L^{p'}(Q)}+\|G_h\overline U_h\|_{L^p(Q)}^{p-1})$, so reflexive weak compactness gives $q_h\rightharpoonup q$ along a further subsequence. The cell averages $b_h$ have the same weak limit: for a smooth vector test $\phi$, $\int(q_h-b_h)\cdot\phi=\sum_{n,K}\int_{I_n\times K}q_h\cdot(\phi-\phi_K)$, whose absolute value is $O(h)\|q_h\|_{p'}\|\nabla_x\phi\|_\infty$. The averages are bounded by Jensen, and density extends this identification to all dual tests. [F1, F2, F4, F5, given, algebra]


2.1 Let $\varphi\in C_c^\infty([0,T)\times\Omega)$. In each step test by $I_h\varphi(t_{n-1})$ and sum after multiplying by $\tau_n$. The gradient part equals $\sum_n\int_{I_n\times\Omega}q_h\cdot G_hI_h\varphi(t_{n-1})$, and replacing the last factor by $\nabla\varphi(t,x)$ costs $O(h+\delta_h)\|q_h\|_{p'}$, by smoothness and [F2]. Weighted Hölder bounds the entire stabilization part by $C\|S_{h,p}(\overline U_h)\|_{L^p}^{p-1}\|S_{h,p}(I_h\varphi(t_{n-1}))\|_{L^p}=O(h)$. Since the test cell values are exact means, discrete summation by parts in the mass term is exact. In fact the summed mass term equals $-\int_Q\Pi_h\overline U_h\partial_t\varphi-\int_\Omega\Pi_hU_h^0\varphi(0)$ exactly, since $\varphi(T)=0$ and the increment $\varphi(t_n)-\varphi(t_{n-1})$ equals its time-derivative integral on each interval. The load converges to $\int_Qf\varphi$: because its cell/time means pair exactly with a cell/time constant test, replacing that test by $\varphi$ costs $O(h+\delta_h)\|f\|_{p'}$. Consequently the actual computed fields satisfy $$-\int_Q\Pi_h\overline U_h\partial_t\varphi+\int_Qq_h\cdot\nabla\varphi-\int_Qf\varphi-\int_\Omega u_0\varphi(0)\longrightarrow0.$$ Passing to the limit gives the corresponding identity with $u,q$. This proves vanishing smooth-test residuals directly from the scheme. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, algebra]


3.1 The limiting identity gives $u'=f+\operatorname{div}q\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, since $|\int fz-q\cdot\nabla z|\le(C_P\|f\|_{p'}+\|q\|_{p'})\|z\|_V$. Density of smooth compactly supported functions in $V$ extends the derivative identity to all $V$ tests. Together with [F1], [F3] gives $u\in C([0,T];H)$. Scalar integration by parts in the limiting identity with tests $\theta(t)z(x)$ identifies $(u(0),z)_H=(u_0,z)_H$ for every smooth compactly supported $z$, hence $u(0)=u_0$. Its energy identity before flux identification is $$\frac12\|u(T)\|_H^2-\frac12\|u_0\|_H^2=\int_Qfu-\int_Qq\cdot\nabla u.$$ [F1, F3, F4, step 2.1, algebra]


4.1 The affine interpolated scalar pairings $(\widehat{\Pi_hU_h}(t),z)_H$ for $z\in V$ have uniformly bounded $L^{p'}$ derivatives and uniform $H$ bounds by [F1]. They are equicontinuous with modulus $C_z|t-s|^{1/p}$, and their distance from the piecewise constant pairings is at most $C_z\delta_h^{1/p}$. Strong time-integrated state convergence identifies their uniform limit as $(u(t),z)_H$; finite-grid compactness followed by uniqueness of this limit justifies taking the uniform limit. At $T$ their values are $(\Pi_hU_h^{N_h},z)_H$. Density of $V$ in $H$ and the uniform terminal bound give $\Pi_hU_h^{N_h}\rightharpoonup u(T)$ in $H$. In particular $\|u(T)\|_H^2\le\liminf_h\|\Pi_hU_h^{N_h}\|_H^2$. [F1, F3, step 3.1, algebra]


5.1 Testing each step by its own state and summing gives the exact identity $$\frac12\|\Pi_hU_h^{N_h}\|_H^2+\frac12\sum_n\|\Pi_h(U_h^n-U_h^{n-1})\|_H^2+\int_Qq_h\cdot G_h\overline U_h+\sum_{n,K,F}\tau_n\alpha_{0,K}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}|\rho_{K,F}(U_h^n)|^p=\frac12\|\Pi_hU_h^0\|_H^2+\int_Qf\Pi_h\overline U_h.$$ The load equality uses that the state is constant on each space-time cell. Its limit is $\int fu$ by strong $L^p(Q)$ convergence. The initial norms converge strongly, and all the jump and stabilization terms are nonnegative. Step 4.1 and the energy identity in step 3.1 therefore give $\limsup_h\int_Qq_h\cdot G_h\overline U_h\le\int_Qq\cdot\nabla u$. Thus [F3] applies to the actual computed $G_h\overline U_h$ and $q_h=a(x,G_h\overline U_h)$, yielding $q=a(x,\nabla u)$ almost everywhere. Steps 2.1–2.2 now give exactly the claimed weak evolution solution. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]


6.1 Pointwise monotonicity compared with the fixed field $\nabla u$ gives $0\le\int_Q(q_h-a(x,\nabla u))\cdot(G_h\overline U_h-\nabla u)$. Expanding and passing through the three weakly linear terms gives $\liminf_h\int q_h\cdot G_h\overline U_h\ge\int q\cdot\nabla u$, because $q=a(x,\nabla u)$. Together with step 5.1 this proves energy convergence. In the exact discrete identity of step 5.1 the right side converges, the flux term now converges, and the terminal norm has the stated lower bound. Hence the sum of the nonnegative jump and stabilization terms tends to zero, and the terminal norms converge to $\|u(T)\|_H$. Weak terminal convergence plus convergence of norms in the real Hilbert space gives strong terminal convergence. The lower bound $\alpha_{0,K}\ge\underline\alpha$ proves $\sum_n\tau_nS_{h,p}(U_h^n)^p\to0$. [F2, F3, step 4.1, step 5.1, algebra]


7.1 For a local face basis, $G_K\phi_{K,F}=|F|n_{K,F}/|K|$ and $\rho_{K,E}(\phi_{K,F})=\mathbf1_{E=F}-(|F|/|K|)n_{K,F}\cdot r_{K,E}$. Substitution into the defined spatial form gives $Q_{K,F}^{\rm nl}=-|F|(b_K-c_K)\cdot n_{K,F}-s_{K,F}$, exactly the stated normal trace of $q_h^{\rm num}$. Pyramid volumes are $|F|\operatorname{dist}(x_K,\operatorname{aff}F)/d\asymp |F|h$, by the shape-regular fan geometry. Since $d_{K,F}\asymp h$, weighted finite-sum Hölder and the bounded face count give $$\int_Q|q_h^{\rm num}-b_h|^{p'}\le C\sum_{n,K,F}\tau_n|F|h^{1-p}|\rho_{K,F}(U_h^n)|^p\le C\sum_n\tau_n S_{h,p}(U_h^n)^p.$$ Indeed the $s_{K,F}/|F|$ term contributes $|F|h(h^{1-p}|\rho|^{p-1})^{p'}=|F|h^{1-p}|\rho|^p$, and $c_K=|K|^{-1}\sum_Fs_{K,F}r_{K,F}$ has the same bound after summing its cell volume. Step 6.1 proves strong vanishing of this difference. Step 1.1 gives $b_h\rightharpoonup q$, so the full numerical reconstruction converges weakly to the asserted physical flux. It need not be continuous across internal pyramid interfaces; the result asserts exactly its physical face normal values and its $L^{p'}$ weak convergence. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 6.1, algebra]


8.1 The weak evolution solution already established above belongs to $L^p(V)\cap L^\infty(H)$. Set $w_h=u$ on the extracted sequence and $\widetilde q_h=a(x,\nabla u)$. Strong computed-state convergence in [F1] gives $\|\Pi_h\overline U_h-w_h\|_{L^p(H)}\to0$. The conforming gradients and recovery fluxes are constant sequences, so their weak convergence and flux-energy limsup are equalities. Define the old lemma's residual using these recovery fluxes. Subtracting the exact weak equation for $u$ leaves just $-\int_Q(\Pi_h\overline U_h-u)\partial_t\varphi$, which tends to zero. Thus every old conditional hypothesis is fulfilled on the bounded open domain. This is an existential limit recovery, not a claim that the computed companion gradients converge strongly or that its nonlinear flux equals the numerical flux; steps 1.1–5.1 supplied the actual scheme closure first. [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, construct, algebra] ∎

**Given:** A fixed polygonal subdomain, a shape-regular quasiuniform matching affine triangulation, a $P_1$ boundary trace $g$, and its local stiffness matrix.

[F1] [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]]: the local energy is $\rho_i\int_{\Omega_i}|\nabla v_h|^2$, and all geometric constants are uniform over the specified family.

[F2] [[def-pe26-discrete-harmonic-extension-and-schur-complement]]: $g^TS_i g$ is the energy of the discrete harmonic extension.

[F3] [[thm-pe26-harmonic-extension-minimizes-energy]]: among all local finite-element lifts of $g$, that extension minimizes the energy.



1.1 On the upper half-plane, Fourier transformation in the tangential variable gives, for a smooth lift $V$ with trace $g$, $$|\xi||\widehat g(\xi)|^2\le\int_0^\infty\bigl(|\partial_t\widehat V(\xi,t)|^2+|\xi|^2|\widehat V(\xi,t)|^2\bigr)\,dt.$$ Indeed, integrate $-\partial_t|\widehat V|^2$ and apply $2ab\le a^2+b^2$. Integration in $\xi$ proves the trace seminorm bound. Conversely, $\widehat V(\xi,t)=e^{-t|\xi|}\widehat g(\xi)$ has gradient energy $\int |\xi||\widehat g(\xi)|^2\,d\xi$. In a bounded chart, multiply the half-plane extension by a fixed cutoff in the inward coordinate; the added gradient term is controlled by the localized L2 boundary norm, hence by the full H1/2 norm after constants are removed. A finite collection of Lipschitz graph charts covers the polygon boundary, including its corners. Flattening each chart is bi-Lipschitz, so it changes the $H^1$ gradient and boundary Gagliardo seminorm by bounded factors. Applying a partition of unity and the half-plane trace inequality to arbitrary chart-localized lifts gives $|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}\le C\|V\|_{H^1(\Omega_i)}$. Subtract the domain mean of $V$ and use scaled Poincar\'e to replace the full $H^1$ norm by $\|\nabla V\|_{L^2}$. In the other direction, apply a partition of unity to boundary data, use the half-plane extensions, and sum to obtain a right inverse of the trace. First subtract a boundary constant; the fractional Poincar\'e inequality on the connected polygon boundary controls the localized full norms by the seminorm. Add that constant back as a constant lift, which has zero gradient. The finite chart count and chart constants are uniform under [F1]. [given, F1, construct, algebra]


1.2 Construct an interpolant $I_h:H^1(\Omega_i)\to V_h$ as follows. For each interior mesh vertex choose one incident triangle and set its coefficient to the average of $V$ on that triangle. For each boundary vertex choose one incident boundary edge and set its coefficient to the integral of the trace of $V$ against the $L^2$-dual function to the endpoint nodal basis on that edge. These dual functionals reproduce every affine edge trace, so the trace of $I_hV$ is exactly $g$ whenever the trace of $V$ is $g$. All coefficients reproduce constants. For a triangle $K$, the chosen elements and edges for its vertices lie in a connected patch $\omega_K$ of diameter at most $Ch$ containing a uniformly bounded number of triangles; these patches have bounded overlap. Let $c_K$ be the mean of $V$ on $\omega_K$. Scaled Poincaré gives $\|V-c_K\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}\le Ch\|\nabla V\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}$, and the scaled trace inequality gives $\|V-c_K\|_{L^2(e)}\le Ch^{1/2}\|\nabla V\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}$ on a selected boundary edge $e$. Thus each interior average coefficient of $V-c_K$ is bounded by $C\|\nabla V\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}$. A boundary dual function has $L^2(e)$ norm at most $Ch^{-1/2}$, so its coefficient has the same bound. Since $I_hc_K=c_K$ and the affine basis functions have uniformly bounded $L^2(K)$ gradient norms in two dimensions, $\|\nabla I_hV\|_{L^2(K)}\le C\|\nabla V\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}$. Summing and using bounded overlap proves $\|\nabla I_hV\|_{L^2(\Omega_i)}\le C\|\nabla V\|_{L^2(\Omega_i)}$. [given, F1, construct, algebra]


2.1 For any finite-element lift $v_h$ of $g$, step 1.1 gives $|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}^2\le C\|\nabla v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega_i)}^2$. Taking the minimum over such lifts and using [F2]–[F3] gives the lower Schur bound. For the upper bound, step 1.1 supplies a continuous lift $V$ with gradient energy at most $C|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}^2$, and step 1.2 gives a boundary-preserving finite-element lift $I_hV$ with the same bound up to a uniform factor. Minimality [F3] bounds the discrete harmonic energy by this lift. Multiplication by $\rho_i$ proves both inequalities. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

**Given:** Finite exact dyadic type-1 or type-2 data, a finite nonempty candidate list satisfying the displayed integer/rational hypotheses, the selected operationwise model and its valid unit-roundoff bound $u$, positive requested tolerance $\varepsilon_{\rm req}$, phase controls $\delta_\phi,p_{\phi,0},p_{\phi,\max},d_{\rm FFT},\epsilon_{\rm tw}$, common range truncation index $J$, and the interval and FFT routines named in the Definition.

[F1] [[def-nufft-transform-types-and-mode-conventions]]: the source, mode and output lists are finite, and the type-1/type-2 formulas use the stated mode set.

[F2] [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]]: each elementary range call uses a finite truncation index $N$ and format, and returns either a finite enclosure or a named failure status; the Definition fixes these to $N=J$ and $(p,e_{\min},e_{\max})$.

[F3] [[alg-na-computed-unitary-radix-two-fft]] and [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]: each FFT call requires input coordinates in its selected model's representable set, uses a positive phase tolerance, finite phase-precision range and recursion cap, and returns a certificate for every used twiddle or a failure status; $u$ is a valid bound for that same model instance.

[F4] [[thm-outward-rounded-operations-are-isotone-and-dag-sound]]: every finite interval operation encloses its exact range; invalid or unbounded operations return a non-finite status.

[F5] [[def-nufft-finite-array-norms]]: the finite $\ell_2$ norms used for grid and mode error radii are defined by finite sums, with value zero on an empty array.

[F6] [[thm-na-computed-unitary-radix-two-fft-error-bound]]: a successful unitary FFT with the selected model's $u\le1/16$ and all used twiddle certificates at most $\epsilon_{\rm tw}\le1/4$ has Euclidean error factor $(1+10u+\epsilon_{\rm tw})^q-1$ at length $2^q$, in either direction. The type-1 radius construction uses the actual center-grid bound $U$ and these checked factors; its scaling by $P^{-1/2}$ and positive mode divisions are included explicitly.



1.1 The elementary evaluator in [F2] visits a finite typed DAG in topological order. Its series have the fixed finite index $J$; its exponential scaling uses a finite integer number of squarings; logarithm bins are a finite integer range determined by positive finite endpoints; and trigonometric reduction examines a finite cell list determined by finite endpoints and a positive certified pi lower bound, returning a named failure if that bound or a branch is unresolved. Square-root endpoint bisection starts with finite integer indices and strictly decreases their positive gap until it is at most one ([[alg-dyadic-square-root-bisection]]). Thus these child calls terminate. The phase routine examines only the integer precisions from $p_{\phi,0}$ to $p_{\phi,\max}$ and calls those finite evaluators ([[alg-na-certified-unit-circle-phase]]). Each FFT recursion either returns at length one, returns when its depth cap is zero, or makes two calls with the cap reduced by one and a finite twiddle loop. Induction on the finite depth cap therefore proves termination of every forward call; inverse mode adds only finite conjugations. A failed child call propagates its named status. Consequently no child in [F2]–[F3] is an unbounded evaluation oracle. [given, F2, F3, F4, induction, algebra]


1.2 Every loop in a candidate is finite: the dimension, source and mode lists, grid-cell lists, image ranges $[-L_r,L_r]$, expression DAGs, range truncation index $J$, phase precision interval $[p_{\phi,0},p_{\phi,\max}]$, and recursion cap $d_{\rm FFT}$ are finite by [F1]–[F3], while every FFT length is a finite power of two by [F3]. The finite norm sums used in the radius construction are defined by [F5]. Thus a candidate either returns a result or reaches one of its explicitly named failure branches after finitely many operations. [given, F1, F2, F3, F5, algebra]


1.3 Every division in step 1 is preceded by the denominator, $s_r<1$, and $d_{\min}^->0$ checks; every type-1 or type-2 mode division is preceded by its own positive-lower-endpoint test in steps 3–4. Hence all performed divisions have divisor intervals excluding zero. The FFT is called only on inputs in its model's representable set; its statuses are checked and no FFT output is used unless every returned twiddle certificate is at most $\epsilon_{\rm tw}$. The type-1 FFT-error radius uses the same checked call bounds [F6]; its normalization divisor is checked to have a strictly positive enclosure before division, and its finite upward radius sum is checked for overflow. A failed interval, range, FFT, denominator, mode-positivity, radius or twiddle check rejects the candidate. Sound containment of every returned finite interval follows from [F2] and [F4]. [given, F2, F3, F4, F6, algebra]


2.1 The ordered candidate list is finite, and processing terminates for each candidate by step 1.2. The procedure returns the first successful candidate whose outward absolute-error bound meets $\varepsilon_{\rm req}$; if none does so, it returns inconclusive with the first recorded non-success reason, including `requested-tolerance-not-met` when all computed bounds exceed tolerance. Therefore every certified return has passed its finite checks, and the inconclusive branch returns no approximation certified to the requested tolerance. [given, F1, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra] ∎

**Given:** An invocation of [[alg-certified-gamma-loggamma-evaluation]] with its finite backend parameters. For enclosure assertions assume a successful return on the admissible rectangle $Z$; termination also covers unsuccessful returns.

[A1] [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]], [[thm-real-elementary-range-enclosures]] and [[thm-complex-elementary-range-enclosures]] give sound finite real and complex elementary outputs. [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]] and [[thm-outward-rounded-operations-are-isotone-and-dag-sound]] preserve containment through the finite arithmetic expressions.

[F1] [[alg-certified-gamma-loggamma-evaluation]] defines the least admissible shift, finite stage cutoffs, actual outward range calls, coordinate enlargements, candidate intersection, final tests and shared work accounting. This is a procedure specification; its correctness is proved below.

[F2] [[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]] defines the absolute-radius and optional zero-excluding relative-radius tests and the four statuses.

[F3] [[lem-loggamma-shift-independent]]: on the slit plane, for an admissible shift $m$,
$$\ell(z)=\ell_+(z+m)-\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\operatorname{Log}(z+j),\qquad \exp(\ell(z))=\Gamma(z).$$

[F4] [[lem-loggamma-series-convergence-and-gamma-identity]]: the series defining $\ell_+$ converges to the stated Gamma branch on the right half-plane. [[lem-loggamma-product-tail-bound]] bounds the tail after $N>2|w|$ terms by $|w|^2/(2N(1-|w|/(N+1)))$.

[F5] [[lem-explicit-euler-constant-enclosure]]: $H_M-\log M-1/M\le\gamma_E\le H_M-\log M$ for $M\ge1$.

[F6] [[lem-sectorial-stirling-explicit-remainder-bound]]: on the right half-plane,
$$\ell_+(w)=(w-\tfrac12)\operatorname{Log}w-w+\tfrac12\log(2\pi)+R(w),\qquad |R(w)|\le\frac1{4|w|}.$$

[F7] [[lem-trigonometric-identities-machin-and-range-reduction]] gives the Machin identity and the finite arctangent tails used to enclose $\pi$.



1.1 For an admissible $Z$, the prescribed integer shift has $a_W=\inf\Re(Z+m)>0$. Translation by a nonnegative real integer preserves cut avoidance: either the imaginary interval omits zero, or the real lower endpoint was already positive. Thus each exact shift-log input lies in its domain. Its outward-rounded input still contains it; the procedure uses it only when its domain is certified. By [A1] the finite shift-log sum therefore encloses the corresponding exact sum for every $z\in Z$. An unavailable shift sum discards the stage and makes no finite claim. [given, A1, F1, F3, algebra]


2.1 Write $G_M=[g_-,g_+]$ for a finite enclosure of $\log M$. By [F5], the outward interval $[H_M-g_+-1/M,H_M-g_-]$ contains the same real $\gamma_E$ used by the branch. Finite outward evaluation of the product partial sum contains its exact value for every $w\in W_Z=Z+m$ by [A1]. The exact rational majorant $R_W$ bounds $|w|$ uniformly. When $N>2R_W$, [F4] bounds each omitted tail by $T_N=R_W^2/(2N(1-R_W/(N+1)))$, since the numerator increases and the positive denominator decreases when $|w|$ is replaced by $R_W$. The disk of radius $T_N$ lies in the coordinate rectangle used to enlarge the partial sum. Subtracting the containing shift-log sum from step 1.1 and using [F3] therefore encloses the full range $\ell(Z)$. [A1, F1, F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]


2.2 The finite Machin construction encloses $\pi$ by [F7]. Its positive interval and the real logarithm call enclose $\log(2\pi)$ by [A1]. Therefore the finite Stirling main-term rectangle contains the exact main term on $W_Z$. For every such $w$, $|w|\ge\Re w\ge a_W>0$, so [F6] gives $|R(w)|\le1/(4a_W)$. The prescribed outward coordinate enlargement contains this remainder disk. After subtracting the shift-log sum, [F3] again identifies every enclosed target as the same continued branch $\ell(z)$. [A1, F1, F3, F6, F7, step 1.1, algebra]


3.1 Either finite log candidate thus contains $\ell(Z)$; their coordinatewise intersection, when used, also contains that entire image. For a log-Gamma target the selected rectangle is therefore sound. For a Gamma target, [A1] encloses its complex exponential, and [F3] identifies the pointwise exponential with $\Gamma(z)$ for every $z\in Z$. This proves full input-range containment for both targets. [A1, F1, F3, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]


4.1 The algorithm tests the actual final outward rectangle's radius before reporting `success`, and sets a relative flag only when the rectangle excludes zero and passes the relative-radius test. By [F2] these arithmetic tests give exactly the stated absolute and reported relative guarantees. Failed or non-finite candidates are never used for a finite success claim; no finite-cap success guarantee is asserted. [F1, F2, step 3.1]


5.1 The stage count is at most $P$, each shift and sum has a finite integer cutoff, and each elementary call has a finite DAG, format and truncation index. Moreover [F1] checks the shared counter before each local or nested primitive operation and loop update, interrupting before either its own or its caller's remaining work budget is exceeded. Consequently every capped invocation returns a status after finitely many charged operations, whether or not any candidate succeeds. [given, F1, A1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** The measurable periodic scalar ellipticity bounds, the corrector cell equation, two-scale compactness and gradient decomposition, periodic averaging, Lax--Milgram, and Countable Choice.

[F1] [[def-periodic-scalar-diffusion-data]]: $a$ is measurable and periodic, $\lambda\le a\le\Lambda$, and the physical coefficient is $a(x/\epsilon)$.

[F2] [[def-periodic-cell-problem]], [[lem-periodic-cell-corrector-wellposedness]], and [[def-periodic-cell-correctors-and-effective-tensor]]: the mean-zero corrector exists uniquely, depends linearly on its vector argument, and defines the flux average $A^*p$.

[F3] [[thm-periodic-effective-tensor-symmetric-elliptic]]: $A^*$ is symmetric and $\lambda I\le A^*\le\Lambda I$.

[F4] [[lem-unit-cube-h01-separability-and-l2-compactness]]: $H^1_0(Q)$ is Hilbert, separable, satisfies $\|v\|_2\le\|\nabla v\|_2$, and bounded sequences are compact in $L^2$.

[F5] [[thm-lax-milgram]]: bounded coercive forms on a Hilbert space have unique weak solutions.

[F6] [[lem-two-scale-gradient-decomposition-for-h01]]: along any $\epsilon_n\to0$, a bounded $H^1_0$ sequence has a subsequence with two-scale gradient limit $\nabla u+\nabla_yu_1$ and $u_n\rightharpoonup u$ in $H^1_0$.

[F7] [[lem-periodic-averaging-on-cube]] and [[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]]: periodic rescalings have uniform $L^2$ bounds and weak cell-mean limits, and Fourier characters are complete in periodic $L^2$.

[F8] [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]: $H^1_0(Q)$ is the norm closure of $C_c^\infty(Q)$, so the homogenized variational identity extends from compactly supported smooth tests.

[F9] [[def-weak-topology-on-a-normed-space]]: weak convergence is convergence under every bounded linear functional.

[F10] [[def-periodic-zero-mean-cell-space]] and [[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]]: $V_\#$ is the $H^1$ closure of smooth periodic functions, and Parseval applies to each smooth periodic function and its first derivatives; step 1.2 proves the required rational trigonometric density from these facts.

[F11] [[lem-smooth-compactly-supported-functions-are-dense-in-ltwo-of-an-open-set]]: $C_c^\infty(Q)$ is dense in $L^2(Q)$.

[F12] [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]: the section integrals used to define $F_w$ are measurable and obey the iterated-integral identities for the integrable products below.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice supplies the subsequences and the countable dense trigonometric test family; neither full Choice nor Dependent Choice is used.






1.1 Equip $H^1_0(Q)$ with gradient norm, equivalent to its Sobolev norm by [F4]. 1.3 Apply [F1] with exact form $a$, exact load $F$, and conforming subspace $X_h$. It gives the unique exact solution $u$, the unique exact Galerkin solution $u_h$, and $\|u-u_h\|_H\le(1+C/c)\inf_{v_h\in X_h}\|u-v_h\|_H$, since the consistency defect is zero. [A1, F1, given, construct]
